answer: A stake-bonded identity registry resists Sybil attacks: each agent must lock a refundable deposit in a vault before it can trade, and its reputation grows like a trellis — each verified transaction adds a rung others can check. New identities start with crystal-clear limits: no history, no credit, tiny trades only. An attacker can still spawn fake agents, but each one costs a fresh locked deposit and months of slow reputation building, so flooding the economy becomes expensive while honest agents keep their bonds.
